info.title: Tron API
info.description: Tron backend API: health, public runtime configuration, the authenticated caller's identity, and (in later tasks) scheduling endpoints.

get.summary:
Public, unauthenticated configuration the frontend needs before it can
authenticate at all (which auth mode, which OIDC issuer/client/scopes).
Deliberately contains no secrets and performs no token validation.

200.description: Public runtime configuration

get.summary:
Liveness check. Unauthenticated by design: infrastructure (load
balancers, orchestrators) must be able to probe this without credentials.

200.description: Service is up

oneOf.description: No delivery with this id was pushed to this connection's session under an unrevoked worker API key. Accept on the connection that received the `work`.
The delivery's `accept_deadline` had passed, including when it had already been marked failed to deliver.

This same delivery was already accepted (or is in flight) or reported, or its run was cancelled. A cancelled run's delivery stays `pushed`; the accept is refused because the run is cancelled. For `one_runner`, another delivery for this run already won the run-scoped accept race. Broadcast modes do not choose a winner.

No `X-Cruma-Org` header was present: the caller is acting in their
own personal context.

The caller named an organization via `X-Cruma-Org` and is an active
member of it.

org_name.description:
The organization's display name as the membership source reports
it. Display only, never a scoping key; absent when the source has
no name to give.

ActingContext.description:
Which organization, if any, the caller is acting as. Derived from the
[`X_CRUMA_ORG`] header by the [`FromRequestParts`] impl below.

# Organization means a verified member

The header is only an assertion. The extractor produces
[`ActingContext::Organization`] solely after the request's
[`OrgMembership`] source answered that the authenticated *user* is an
active member of that organization; every other outcome is a refusal
(see [`ActingContextRejection`]). So the value is safe to scope data by,
and it still carries no *role*: membership is all it proves.

Values built by hand (repository tests, for instance) are not verified;
only the extractor guarantees membership.

oneOf.description: The job's most recently created run; absent when it never ran.

AdminLastRunResponse.description:
The state of a job's latest run. Carries no delivery detail, runner
credentials or result data.

job_count.description: Jobs the scope owns that are not deleted; zero when it has none.

counts.description: One entry per distinct requested scope, in the order first requested.

AdminToggleEvidence.description:
Evidence available to Tron about the owner's feature toggle. Organizations
are `Unknown` until cruma-web-api exposes an organization-level lookup.

ApiErrorBody.description:
Error body returned by the API namespace. Typed rather than assembled as
JSON at the call site (ADR-2).

`message` is human-readable detail for whoever is reading the response by
hand; clients branch on [`ApiErrorBody::error`], never on the prose. It is
omitted from the wire entirely when there is nothing useful to add beyond
the code.

ApiErrorCode.description:
Machine-readable discriminant for [`ApiErrorBody::error`]. ADR-1: an
enum, not a bare string, so clients match on a value the compiler knows.

AuthMode.description:
How the backend authenticates requests.

* [`AuthMode::Dev`] — no OIDC configuration read at all, permissive CORS,
  and bearer tokens are **not verified**: the `dev.<subject>` bypass in
  [`crate::auth`] is live. Intended for local development only.
* [`AuthMode::Oidc`] — requires `AUTH_ISSUER`, `AUTH_JWKS_URI` and
  `AUTH_CLIENT_ID` (all three are read by `umbra-auth`'s
  `AuthConfig::from_env`; see [`crate::config::AuthSettings`]) and
  enforces an explicit CORS origin allow-list.

ConnectedSessionIdentity.description:
What a connected runner announced about itself. Every field is the
runner's own claim and optional; a runner that never announced has none.

CreatedWorkerApiKeyResponse.description:
Body of a successful `POST /api/worker-api-keys`: the key's metadata and
its clear-text token. This is the only response that ever carries the
token; the server keeps only a salted one-way digest of it.

token.description:
The credential a worker presents to authenticate. Shown once; it
cannot be retrieved again, only revoked and replaced.

DatabaseHealthStatus.description: Reachability of the configured Postgres pool at probe time.

DeliveryAttempt.description:
Which attempt of a run's delivery slot a delivery row is. The first push is
attempt 1; each retry is the previous attempt plus one.

DurationSummaryResponse.description: Distribution of one duration over the samples that had it.

p50_ms.description: Nearest-rank median, absent when there are no samples.

p90_ms.description: Nearest-rank 90th percentile, absent when there are no samples.

samples.description: How many runs or deliveries had the timestamps this duration needs.

EffectiveNotificationRules.description: The rule that actually applies to a job.

HealthStatus.description:
Discriminant for [`HealthResponse::status`]. ADR-1: an enum, not a bare
`"ok"` string literal set at the handler call site.

JobDeliveryMode.description:
Typed runner delivery contract.  It replaces the legacy fan-out pair so
clients cannot combine a dispatch policy with an incompatible threshold.

JobLastRunResponse.description:
How a job's most recent run stands. Carries no delivery detail, runner
credentials or result data.

finished_at.description: Absent while the run is still open.

JobMissedRun.description: What to do when a runner is unavailable at a scheduled time.

JobNotificationRulesResponse.description: A job's own notification setting and what applies to it after inheritance.

oneOf.description: The job's own rule or opt-out; absent when it inherits.
The job has its own rule; the owner default is ignored for it.
The job is explicitly excluded from the owner default.

JobNotificationSetting.description: What a job itself says about notifications.

JobNotificationWrite.description: A job's PUT body: its own rule, or an opt-out of the owner default.

JobRequest.description: Full, typed configuration accepted when creating or replacing a job.

miss_grace_seconds.description: Null retains the scheduler-published default window.

overlap_policy.description: What to do when an occurrence is due while an earlier run is active.

retry_policy.description:
Attempts, backoff and retryable failures for runner deliveries. Omitted
means no retries.

time_zone.description: IANA time-zone name used to interpret cron schedules. Null means UTC.

JobResponse.description:
Safe, client-visible job configuration. It intentionally contains no
runner credentials, delivery acceptance secrets, or opaque result data.

deleted_at.description:
When the owner deleted the job; absent for a live job. A deleted job
keeps its run history, is never scheduled or triggered, and can be
restored.

effective_miss_grace_seconds.description: Configured missed-start window, with the scheduler default resolved.

oneOf.description:
The job's most recently created run, derived when the job is read.
Absent when the job never ran.

next_run_at.description:
When the scheduler will next create a run for this job, which is what
a countdown should count down to. At or before the current time it
means an occurrence is already due and awaiting the scheduler's next
pass. Absent when the schedule has no further occurrence.

public_id.description:
The identifier of the job's public page. It identifies the job to the
public only while `visibility` is `public`.

time_zone.description: IANA time-zone name used to interpret cron schedules. Null means UTC.

visibility.description: Whether anyone holding the public URL can read the job's status.

JobRunPageResponse.description: A page of the owner-visible history for one job.

JobRunResponse.description:
One execution record of a job. Carries no runner credentials, delivery
secrets or opaque result data.

attempts.description:
Each outbound request a webhook run made, oldest first. Only on
responses about one of the caller's own jobs. Empty for runner runs,
for runs not yet claimed, and for runs that pre-date the attempt ledger
(read those from the run's own `status`, `failure_kind`,
`http_status_code` and `delivery_duration_ms`).

deliveries.description:
Each push of this run to a runner, oldest first. Empty for webhook
runs and for runs not yet pushed.

delivery_duration_ms.description: How long the webhook request took, in milliseconds.

oneOf.description: How a failed or timed-out run went wrong.

http_status_code.description: The HTTP status a webhook answered with, when it answered at all.

late_at.description:
When the run was first seen open, or finished, past the job's
lateness threshold. Its status is unaffected.

oneOf.description:
How the run's status follows from its deliveries under the job's
delivery mode. Absent for runs with no delivery (see `status_reason`),
and on responses that are not about one of the caller's jobs.

Why the run is in a policy-driven state, e.g. a missed occurrence that
was skipped or deferred. Absent for ordinary runs.

timings.description: Durations derived from this run and its deliveries' durable timestamps.

runners.description: Ordered by runner name. Empty for a job whose recent runs reached no runner.

window_runs.description:
How many of the job's newest runs were examined; at most
[`RECENT_RUN_COUNT`].

JobSchedule.description:
A future execution schedule. Intervals are expressed in whole seconds so
they round-trip precisely through Postgres' checked integer column.

JobTarget.description: Where a job sends its run. Webhook URLs are never used for runner jobs.

buckets.description: Ascending; buckets without a completed run are omitted.

runners.description: Ordered by runner name. Empty for a webhook job.

JobVisibilityRequest.description: Whether a job's public page is reachable.

oneOf.description: A pre-announce runner. It is eligible for every handler this release.

concurrency_capacity.description: Effective compatibility capacity for this release.

current_load.description: Durable unfinished deliveries assigned to this session.

worker_api_key_id.description: Worker API key that authenticated this live session.

oneOf.description: A runner that sent one validated capability announcement.

concurrency_capacity.description: Positive maximum number of concurrent deliveries this session accepts.

current_load.description: Durable unfinished deliveries assigned to this session.

display_name.description: Optional human-readable name supplied by the runner.

handler_keys.description: Stable handler keys this runner can execute.

oneOf.description: Typed protocol version supplied by the runner.

runner_version.description: Optional implementation version supplied by the runner.

sdk_version.description: Optional SDK version supplied by the runner.

worker_api_key_id.description: Worker API key that authenticated this live session.

LiveRunnerSession.description:
How Tron lists a currently connected runner session to its owner, by
`kind`: `legacy` when the runner never sent `announce`, `announced` once it
did. Live only; nothing here is stored.

MeResponse.description:
Body of `GET /api/me`: who the bearer token says the caller is, and which
organization they are acting in for this request.

acting.description:
Resolved from the `X-Cruma-Org` request header; absent header means
[`ActingContext::Personal`]. A named organization appears here only
after the caller was verified as an active member of it.

subject.description:
The token subject: `sub` for a user, the service id for a machine
identity. Stable across requests and safe to key on.

MissGraceWindow.description:
The server-owned bounds and fallback for a job's missed-start window.
Published through typed API responses so clients never copy scheduler
timing rules.

org_member_subjects.description:
Organization members chosen by subject; only valid for an
organization's rules. Resolved to addresses when sending.

has_signing_secret.description: Whether a signing secret is stored. The value is never returned.

id.description:
An existing channel of this rule to update; needed for
`signing_secret` `keep` to retain its secret.

NotificationRule.description: A stored rule as the API shows it. Secret values are never part of it.

reminder_interval_seconds.description:
While a failure/miss/late condition persists, repeat the notification
at this interval (seconds). Absent: notify once.

events.description: Events to notify on; at least one, duplicates ignored.

OrgId.description:
An organization identifier, as named by the caller via the
[`X_CRUMA_ORG`] header.

This value reaches logs and (eventually) database lookups, so it is
constrained to an opaque identifier charset at the edge -- ASCII
alphanumerics, `-`, and `_` only -- via [`FromStr`], rather than being
sanitised individually at each place it is later used.

PrincipalKind.description:
Which kind of principal a bearer token identified. ADR-1: an enum, not a
bare string — `umbra-auth` genuinely resolves two different things (an
interactive user and a machine/service identity) and collapsing them into
one indistinguishable shape would lose that at the API boundary.

oneOf.description: A frame was not JSON for any runner frame (an unknown `type`, a missing or extra field, including a handler key that does not match the published handler-key schema), or was a binary frame.
Reserved; not sent today. A first frame other than `authenticate` is answered with `authentication_failed`.
`authenticate` was sent again on an authenticated connection.

The announcement broke a constraint: zero capacity; no, too many, duplicate, blank or oversized handler keys; a blank or oversized display name or runner version; or a blank, oversized or non-semver SDK version.
`announce` was sent twice on one connection. Reconnect to replace the announcement.

ProtocolViolation.description: How an authenticated runner broke the protocol.

PublicConfig.description:
Body of `GET /api/config`. Tells the frontend how to authenticate, and
where runners connect.

compatibility_handler_key.description:
Compatibility key for a new runner job until the owner selects a
capability advertised by a connected runner.

dev_token_prefix.description:
The prefix a dev-mode bearer token must carry for
[`crate::auth`]'s bypass to accept the rest of it as the subject —
[`crate::auth::DEV_TOKEN_PREFIX`]. `None` in
[`AuthMode::Oidc`], where no such bypass exists.

Published rather than left for the SPA to hard-code because tron has
no dev-login endpoint to mint one (unlike ai-board): the SPA builds
the token itself, and ADR-1 is explicit that the same const living in
two projects means it belongs in a generated client instead. It is a
dev-only affordance and discloses nothing — in dev mode any caller
who can reach the port can already impersonate anyone, prefix known
or not, and in OIDC mode this is `None` and the bypass is not wired.

miss_grace_window.description: Server-owned missed-start timing rules used by the generated job editor.

retry_policy_window.description: Server-owned retry-policy bounds and default used by the generated job editor.

runner_authentication_timeout_seconds.description:
Seconds a runner has, after opening the WebSocket, to send its
`authenticate` frame before the server answers
`authentication_failed` and closes the connection —
[`crate::runner_socket::AUTHENTICATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`].

runner_result_message_limit_bytes.description:
Bytes of a runner's `report` result message that are kept; a longer
message is cut and marked, never rejected —
[`RetentionSettings::max_result_message_bytes`].

runner_socket_path.description:
The path, on the API's own origin, where runners open their
WebSocket — [`crate::runner_socket::path`]. That route is not an
OpenAPI operation (it is a protocol, not a request/response), so it is
published here for the SPA's connection instructions rather than
copied into the frontend by hand (ADR-1, ADR-3).

PublicDeliveryResponse.description: One push of a run to a runner, without saying which runner.

oneOf.description: The newest run still in progress, pushed to a runner or not.

The newest run that has ended, skipped occurrences included, so it
always agrees with `runs`: absent only while no run has ended.

next_run_at.description:
What a countdown should count down to; absent when the schedule has no
further occurrence.

runs.description: The newest runs first, including skipped occurrences.

PublicRunResponse.description: One run as a visitor sees it.

oneOf.description: No delivery with this id belongs to the reporting worker API key, or that key is revoked.
The secret does not match the one issued in `accepted`, or the delivery was never accepted, so no secret was issued.
The secret matched, but the delivery already has its one final report.

backoff.description: Whether the wait stays at the base or doubles per attempt.

backoff_seconds.description:
Seconds to wait after the first failed attempt; the base the backoff
kind grows from.

max_attempts.description: Total attempts per run, the first one included. 1 means no retries.

max_backoff_seconds.description: The longest wait between two attempts, whichever backoff kind is used.

on_accept_timeout.description: Runner jobs: retry when a pushed delivery is not accepted in time.

on_disconnect.description:
Runner jobs: treat a runner disconnecting mid-run as a failed attempt
and retry it.

on_err.description: Runner jobs: retry when the runner reports `Err`.

on_interrupted.description:
Webhook jobs: re-send an attempt whose outcome is unknown because Tron
stopped while the request was in flight. Only safe when the receiver
deduplicates on `Tron-Delivery-Id`, so it is an explicit opt-in; without
it such a run stays failed and is never re-sent.

on_network_error.description:
Webhook jobs: retry when the request could not reach the receiver or
the connection broke before a response.

on_retryable_status.description:
Webhook jobs: retry on a 5xx, 408 or 429 answer. A `Retry-After` header
on the answer is honoured when it still fits the run's window.

on_timeout.description: Webhook jobs: retry when the receiver does not answer in time.

record_response_excerpt.description:
Webhook jobs: keep a bounded, redacted excerpt of each response body
on its attempt record. Off means no response body is ever stored.

response_excerpt_max_bytes.description: Webhook jobs: the most bytes of response body an excerpt keeps.

RetryPolicyWindow.description:
The server-owned bounds and default for a job's retry policy. Published
through the public config so the editor never copies these numbers.

default_policy.description: The policy a new job starts with: one attempt, no retries.

RevealedWebhookSigningSecretResponse.description: One-time create/rotate response. Copy `secret` immediately: later reads expose only metadata.

RunCancellationRefusal.description:
Typed detail returned when a run has already advanced beyond the owner
cancellation window.  The status lets a generated client distinguish an
accepted runner run from one whose execution is already running.

RunDeliveryResponse.description:
One push of a run to a runner, as its owner sees it. Carries no
acceptance secret; the public page drops the runner name and message.

accept_deadline.description: The instant after which an unaccepted push counts as failed to deliver.

attempt.description:
Which attempt of its delivery slot this push is. Rows written before
retries existed read as attempt 1.

oneOf.description:
What that runner announced about itself, while its connection is still
open. Absent once it has disconnected: Tron keeps no announcement
beyond the connection.

Why the attempt failed, when the failure is one a retry policy can
select. Absent on rows written before retries existed.
How the runner reported the run ending, once it has.

outcome_message.description: The message the runner sent with its `Ok`/`Err` report, once it has.

previous_delivery_id.description: The failed attempt this push retries; absent on first attempts.

retry_due_at.description:
When the retry of this failed attempt is due. Present only until that
retry is pushed or abandoned.

runner_name.description: Name of the worker API key whose runner received the push.

runner_session_id.description:
The runner connection the push went to. Retained with the delivery, so
every row has one, including rows written before retries existed.

timings.description: Durations derived from this delivery and its parent run's timestamps.

RunListFilter.description:
Which runs a listing is narrowed to. Defined over the stored run
vocabulary ([`RunStatus`], [`RunStatusReason`]) rather than a parallel set
of states, so a client filtering by it and a client reading a run's own
fields can never disagree about what a run is.

RunOutcome.description:
The result a runner reports: exactly one of `ok` or `err`, each carrying
a single string, so it serializes as `{"ok": "..."}` or `{"err": "..."}`.

RunStatusDerivation.description:
How a runner run's status follows from the job's delivery mode and the
run's deliveries. Computed with the dispatcher's own settlement rule from
the job's CURRENT configuration, so it can disagree with `status` when the
delivery mode changed after the run ended or the run was cancelled.

completed_successes.description: Delivery slots whose last attempt reported `ok`.

failed_slots.description: Slots whose last attempt failed, with no retry left or selected.

max_attempts.description: Attempts the job's retry policy allows per slot, the first included.

open_attempts.description: Attempts, across all slots, that have not finished.

open_slots.description: Slots whose last attempt is still pushed, accepted or in flight.

required_successes.description: `ok` reports the run needs to succeed.

retry_scheduled_slots.description: Slots whose last attempt failed and whose retry is scheduled.

oneOf.description: The status the settlement rule gives now; `None` while the run waits.

terminal_attempts.description: Attempts, across all slots, that have finished.

undelivered_slots.description:
Slots whose last attempt was never accepted, with no retry left or
selected.

RunTimingResponse.description:
Canonical, nullable timing fields shared by private and public run and
runner-delivery responses. Values are signed millisecond differences
between the persisted lifecycle timestamps; absent endpoints stay absent.

accept_wait_ms.description: Runner push until acceptance. Webhooks have no acceptance phase.

execution_ms.description: Acceptance/request start until the runner report/webhook response.

queue_wait_ms.description: Scheduled occurrence until the first runner push or webhook request.

total_ms.description: Scheduled occurrence until the run or delivery finished.

RunVerdict.description: Where the settlement rule stands for a run's current delivery slots.

RunnerActivityResponse.description: One runner key's share of the job's recent runs.

failed.description: Runs whose last attempt reported err.

failed_to_deliver.description: Runs whose last attempt was never accepted.

oneOf.description: Why the key's latest attempt failed, when a retry policy could select it.

open.description: Runs still pushed, accepted or in flight on this key.

retried_attempts.description: Attempts beyond the first, across the recent runs.

runs.description: Recent runs this key received a delivery for.

succeeded.description: Of those, runs whose last attempt reported ok.

RunnerAnnouncement.description: What a runner declares about its connection in `announce`.

concurrency_capacity.description: Maximum concurrent work this session accepts; it must be positive. Omitted values default to 1 for compatibility with older runners.

display_name.description:
Optional human-readable name shown to the owner; a supplied value is
non-blank and at most 128 bytes long.

handler_keys.description:
Stable handler keys the runner can execute. The set must contain 1 to
128 unique keys, each 1–128 bytes and matching
`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*`.

oneOf.description: Typed version of Tron's runner protocol understood by this session.

runner_version.description:
Optional runner implementation version, retained as display metadata;
a supplied value is non-blank and at most 128 bytes long.

sdk_version.description:
Optional semantic SDK version, used by the server to report whether
this session is older than a peer. A supplied value must parse as a
semantic version and be non-blank and at most 128 bytes long.

RunnerCapabilities.description:
Owner-scoped readiness data for the handler picker. The server, not the
UI, decides which live sessions are stale relative to their peers.

compatibility_handler_key.description:
Compatibility handler assigned to pre-capability jobs. Sessions that
never announced and sessions that announced it are capable of it.

display_name.description: Optional human-readable name the runner announced for itself.

out_of_date.description:
True when this session is legacy, lacks a handler announced by a peer,
or declares an older SDK/protocol version than a peer.

worker_api_key_name.description: Name the owner gave the worker API key that authenticated this session.

RunnerHandlerKey.description:
Stable, validated name of a runner handler.  Handler keys are durable job
configuration, rather than a free-form label inferred from live sessions.

oneOf.description:
Must be the first frame on a new connection. Anything else, or no
frame in time, is answered with `authentication_failed` and the
connection is closed.

token.description:
The worker API key token shown once when the key was created on
the Runners page.

oneOf.description:
Optional, at most once per connection, after `authenticated`: declares
what this runner can do. Tron answers `announced`. Runners that never
announce are listed as legacy sessions and still receive work.

Takes on a delivery Tron pushed with `work`. Send it straight away,
before the delivery's `accept_deadline`. Tron answers `accepted` or
`accept_refused`.

The one final result of an accepted delivery. It may be sent on any
connection authenticated with the same worker API key, for example a
new one after the runner restarted. Tron answers `report_recorded` or
`report_rejected`.

secret.description: The secret from the `accepted` frame for this delivery.

RunnerMessage.description: Frames a runner sends to Tron.

RunnerProtocolVersion.description: A version of the runner protocol defined by Tron.

RunnerTimingResponse.description: Runner deliveries received by one worker API key for the completed runs.

ScopeKey.description:
One customer scope as the admin reads key it: a personal owner's user
public id, or a shared organization's public id.

oneOf.description:
Answers a valid `authenticate`. Several runner processes may
authenticate with the same worker API key at once; each connection
gets its own session.

worker_api_key_id.description: The worker API key the token belongs to.

oneOf.description: Confirms that this connection's `announce` was retained.

The first frame was not a valid `authenticate` in time: a timeout, a
malformed or non-text frame, another frame type, or an unknown,
revoked or mismatched token. The connection is closed right after.

A run has been dispatched to this connection as one delivery. It
carries no job input or payload: only ids, the job's name, the handler
key it was dispatched for and times.

accept_deadline.description:
`accept` must arrive by this time. It is the push time plus the
job's delivery timeout.

delivery_id.description: Names this delivery; echo it in `accept` and `report`.

handler_key.description:
The job's runner handler key. For a connection that announced
handler keys it is one of them; a connection that never announced
receives work for every key. A runner with several handlers runs
the one with this key.

job_name.description: The job's name, as the owner set it.

run_id.description: The run this delivery belongs to.

oneOf.description:
Answers a successful `accept`. Keep the secret: it is shown here
once and never again, and `report` must echo it.

secret.description: The one-time secret for this delivery's `report`.

oneOf.description: Answers an `accept` Tron would not take. Do not run the job.
Answers a `report` Tron recorded. The delivery is finished.

late.description:
True when the report arrived more than the job's lateness
threshold after the run's `scheduled_for`. A late report is
still recorded.

oneOf.description: Answers a `report` Tron could not record.

delivery_id.description: The delivery named in the report.

oneOf.description:
An authenticated runner sent a frame the protocol does not allow. The
connection stays open.

ServerMessage.description: Frames Tron sends to a runner.

oneOf.description: Keep the secret of the channel named by `id` (none if it had none).
Store no signing secret.
Store this value (write-only; it is never returned).

SigningSecretChange.description: What to do with a webhook channel's signing secret on write.

TimingBucket.description: The width of one graph bucket, aligned to UTC.

TimingBucketResponse.description: Completed runs of one bucket, by the instant each run finished.

TimingMetricsResponse.description: Execution and total durations over one set of runs or deliveries.

execution.description: Acceptance (or webhook request start) until the report or response.

total.description: Scheduled occurrence until the run or delivery finished.

WebhookAttemptResponse.description:
One outbound request of a webhook run: when it was made and how it ended.
Never carries the URL, a header or signing value, or error text from the
HTTP stack; the only free text is the response excerpt, which is present
only while the job opts in to keeping one.

delivery_id.description:
The `Tron-Delivery-Id` the receiver saw. It is the run's id and is the
same on every attempt of the run, so a receiver can de-duplicate.

oneOf.description: How a failed attempt went wrong.

http_status_code.description: The HTTP status the receiver answered with, when it answered at all.

response_excerpt.description:
A bounded, redacted piece of the response body. Absent unless the job
currently opts in to recording one.

retry_due_at.description: When the next attempt was scheduled, if this one earned a retry.

WebhookDeliveryIdentity.description: Meaning of the stable delivery identifier.

WebhookPayload.description: The body POSTed to a webhook that has no body template configured.

WebhookSignatureAlgorithm.description: Algorithm used to authenticate webhook deliveries.

WebhookSignatureEncoding.description: Wire encoding of each member in `Tron-Signature`.

WebhookSignatureVerificationResponse.description:
Canonical, server-generated example of the exact bytes and headers a
receiver verifies. The fixture values live here so clients cannot drift
from the real serializer, signer, or header vocabulary.

WebhookSigningSecretResponse.description: Redacted delivery-HMAC signing-secret version metadata. It never contains plaintext.

WebhookSigningSecretStatus.description: Client-visible validity of a redacted webhook delivery signing-secret version.

name.description: A label for the owner to recognise the worker by; not secret.

WorkerApiKeyResponse.description:
Metadata identifying a worker API key. Contains no secret material: the
token, its salt and its digest are never part of this shape.

WorkerApiKeyStatus.description: Whether a worker API key can still authenticate a runner.

zitadel_bearer.description: An access token issued by the Zitadel instance advertised at GET /api/config. Verified locally against the issuer's JWKS.
